raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #45400.

On a hybrid GDN model with `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, host-tier hits drop to zero once the evicted working set is a few long prefixes larger than the device pool. The KV pages are still on host, but identical requests get `cached_tokens: 0` and a full recompute.

A host prefix hit ends at the deepest node on the matched path that still has a Mamba state (device or host). Host Mamba eviction (`drive_host_eviction`) is plain LRU, and a long prefill backs up many chunk checkpoints along one path. With few host Mamba slots, newer intermediate checkpoints evict the tail states of earlier documents, so their host KV is left with no usable Mamba state. `--mamba-max-states-per-path` doesn't help, because it only trims device states after they've been backed up.

## Modifications

- `unified_cache/components/mamba.py` and `rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/components/mamba.rs`: host Mamba eviction now runs in two LRU passes. The first pass evicts only pass-through checkpoints (a node with one child that holds its own Mamba state, on device or host). The second pass, which runs only if the first one didn't free enough, is the existing LRU order. Path tails, forks, and states whose child has no state are kept until no pass-through checkpoint is left, so each path keeps the state its host hit ends at. This matches what `_evict_excess_path_states` already preserves on device.
- The Python and Rust cores get the same change.
- `components/README.md`: describes the new order under `drive_host_eviction()`.
- Tests, in both cores:
  - a pass-through checkpoint is evicted before an older tail
  - a fork is kept until the fallback pass
  - a state whose child has no state is kept
  - eviction falls back to LRU order once no pass-through is left

  Python: `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mamba_host_eviction_order.py` (CPU). Rust: `rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/tests/components/mamba.rs`.

## Accuracy Tests

Answers are unchanged: all 24 responses across the three runs below return the correct passphrase. This change only affects which host Mamba states are evicted, not model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

1x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, driver 595.91.07, image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261029-c10e0e17`. The sglang tree was checked out at this PR's base (`97483164`) for "before" and at this commit for "after", with the Rust core rebuilt for each. Model `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, launched with the flags from the issue minus PP and EAGLE:

```
sglang serve --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code --port 30000 \
  --json-model-override-args '{"language_model_only": true}' \
  --context-length 262144 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --chunked-prefill-size 1024 --mem-fraction-static 0.95 --max-total-tokens 262144 \
  --max-running-requests 4 --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 3 4 --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --max-mamba-cache-size 16 \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 15 --mamba-max-states-per-path 5 \
  --enable-cache-report --enable-metrics
```

Host pools: 396,247 KV tokens and 26 Mamba state slots. Client: `repro.py 4` from the issue (4 × ~89k-token documents, then an identical re-ask of each), with a fresh server per run.

| | before (main, Rust core) | after (Rust core) | after (Python core) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cached_tokens` per re-ask | 0 | 89,088–89,280 | 89,088–89,280 |
| re-ask latency | 16.68–16.70 s | 0.21–0.41 s | 0.21–0.26 s |
| `prefill_effective_tokens_total{mode="host_hit"}` | 0 | 356,672 | 356,672 |
| `hicache_backup_tokens_total{pool="mamba"}` | 702 | 351 | 351 |
| `hicache_host_used_tokens` | 355,447 | 356,663 | 356,663 |

### Before (main `97483164`, Rust core)

```
doc0 first 89294 21.28 0 'pass-0'
doc1 first 89200 16.92 0 'pass-1'
doc2 first 89117 17.13 0 'pass-2'
doc3 first 89195 16.97 0 'pass-3'
doc0 again (identical) 89294 16.7 0 'pass-0'
doc1 again (identical) 89200 16.69 0 'pass-1'
doc2 again (identical) 89117 16.7 0 'pass-2'
doc3 again (identical) 89195 16.68 0 'pass-3'
```

### After (this PR, Rust core)

```
doc0 first 89294 17.17 0 'pass-0'
doc1 first 89200 16.89 0 'pass-1'
doc2 first 89117 16.9 0 'pass-2'
doc3 first 89195 16.94 0 'pass-3'
doc0 again (identical) 89294 0.41 89280 'pass-0'
doc1 again (identical) 89200 0.28 89152 'pass-1'
doc2 again (identical) 89117 0.21 89088 'pass-2'
doc3 again (identical) 89195 0.21 89152 'pass-3'
```

### After (this PR, Python core, `SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python`)

```
doc0 again (identical) 89294 0.26 89280 'pass-0'
doc1 again (identical) 89200 0.26 89152 'pass-1'
doc2 again (identical) 89117 0.21 89088 'pass-2'
doc3 again (identical) 89195 0.21 89152 'pass-3'
```

Columns: label, prompt tokens, request time (s), `cached_tokens`, answer. Cold requests take about 17 s in every run.

### Follow-up

Once no pass-through checkpoint is left, eviction falls back to plain LRU, so tails can still be evicted under heavy pressure, for example branch-heavy sub-agent workloads. A minimum-token-distance rule for keeping pass-through checkpoints is being discussed in the issue. This PR keeps to the reproduced case.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -286,7 +286,7 @@ Each component implements these hooks. See `base.py` for the ABC and docstrings.
 | `evict_component(target=EvictLayer.DEVICE)` | Free this component's device, host, or both resources on a node being evicted. Internal device eviction tombstones (`value = None`); host eviction clears `host_value`. Returns `(device_freed, host_freed)`. | `_evict_component_and_detach_lru` | *abstract* |

Full: leaf-set heap. SWA/Mamba: component LRUs with internal tombstones and atomic leaf deletion. | `UnifiedRadixCache._evict_components` | *abstract* |
-| `drive_host_eviction()` | Drive host eviction for this component, collecting freed values for the Controller to drain. Full uses host leaves; SWA/Mamba use host LRUs. | `evict_host` | no-op |
+| `drive_host_eviction()` | Drive host eviction for this component, collecting freed values for the Controller to drain. Full uses host leaves; SWA/Mamba use host LRUs. Mamba first sweeps its host LRU for pass-through checkpoints (one child that holds its own state) and only then evicts leaves, forks and other states in LRU order, so a path keeps the state its host hit ends at. | `evict_host` | no-op |

         Internal nodes: private tombstone (free host mamba only).
-        Host leaves: atomic eviction via _evict_host_leaf."""

+
+        Pass-through checkpoints go first. A host prefix hit ends at the deepest
+        Mamba state on the matched path, so evicting a path's last state drops
+        the hit for all of its host KV. A pass-through checkpoint has one child
+        that holds its own state, so evicting it only loses hits that end
+        exactly there. Leaves, forks and states with no stateful child are kept

+"""CPU-only unit tests for the Mamba host eviction order."""
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci, register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=5, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+import unittest
+from collections import defaultdict
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_cache.components.base import ComponentType
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_cache.components.mamba import MambaComponent
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_radix_cache import UnifiedLRUList, UnifiedTreeNode
+
+MAMBA = ComponentType.MAMBA
+
+
+class _FakeTreeCore:
+    tree_components = (ComponentType.FULL, ComponentType.MAMBA)
+    enable_session_radix_cache = False
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.root_node = UnifiedTreeNode(self.tree_components)
+        self.evictable_host_leaves = set()
+        self.host_lru_lists = {
+            MAMBA: UnifiedLRUList(MAMBA, self.tree_components, use_host_ptr=True)
+        }
+        self.evicted = []
+
+    def _evict_component_and_detach_lru(
+        self, node, component, *, target, tracker, device_frees, host_frees, **_
+    ):
+        # Host tombstone: free the slot and leave the host LRU.
+        cd = node.component_data[MAMBA]
+        host_frees[MAMBA].append(cd.host_value)
+        cd.host_value = None
+        self.host_lru_lists[MAMBA].remove_node(node)
+        tracker[MAMBA] += 1
+        self.evicted.append(node)
+
+    def _cascade_evict(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        pass
+
+    def _update_evictable_leaf_sets(self, node):
+        pass
+
+
+def _component(core):
+    component = object.__new__(MambaComponent)
+    component.tree_core = core
+    return component
+
+
+def _child(core, parent, key):
+    node = UnifiedTreeNode(core.tree_components)
+    node.parent = parent
+    parent.children[key] = node
+    return node
+
+
+def _chain(core, length):
+    nodes, parent = [], core.root_node
+    for index in range(length):
+        parent = _child(core, parent, index)
+        nodes.append(parent)
+    return nodes
+
+
+def _seed_host_lru(core, nodes):
+    """Give `nodes` host Mamba slots 10, 11, ... in LRU order (first is least recent)."""
+    for index, node in enumerate(nodes):
+        node.component_data[MAMBA].host_value = torch.tensor([10 + index])
+        core.host_lru_lists[MAMBA].insert_mru(node)
+
+
+def _drive(core, num_tokens):
+    tracker = defaultdict(int)
+    host_frees = defaultdict(list)
+    _component(core).drive_host_eviction(
+        num_tokens, tracker, defaultdict(list), host_frees, []
+    )
+    freed = [value.item() for value in host_frees[MAMBA]]
+    assert tracker[MAMBA] == len(freed)
+    return freed
+
+
+def _has_host_state(node):
+    return node.component_data[MAMBA].host_value is not None
+
+
+class TestMambaHostEvictionOrder(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_pass_through_checkpoint_goes_before_an_older_tail(self):
+        core = _FakeTreeCore()
+        a, tail = _chain(core, 2)
+        # The tail is least recent; plain LRU order would evict it first.
+        _seed_host_lru(core, [tail, a])
+
+        self.assertEqual(_drive(core, 1), [11])
+        self.assertFalse(_has_host_state(a))
+        self.assertTrue(_has_host_state(tail))
+        self.assertTrue(core.host_lru_lists[MAMBA].in_list(tail))
+
+    def test_fork_is_kept_until_the_fallback_pass(self):
+        core = _FakeTreeCore()
+        fork, left = _chain(core, 2)
+        passing = _child(core, fork, "right")
+        right = _child(core, passing, "leaf")
+        # The fork is least recent but shared by both branches.
+        _seed_host_lru(core, [fork, left, right, passing])
+
+        self.assertEqual(_drive(core, 1), [13])
+        self.assertFalse(_has_host_state(passing))
+        for node in (fork, left, right):
+            self.assertTrue(_has_host_state(node))
+
+    def test_state_whose_child_has_none_is_kept(self):
+        core = _FakeTreeCore()
+        p, a, _stateless, tail = _chain(core, 4)
+        # `a` is the deepest state of every hit that ends inside `_stateless`.
+        _seed_host_lru(core, [a, tail, p])
+
+        self.assertEqual(_drive(core, 1), [12])
+        self.assertTrue(_has_host_state(a))
+        self.assertTrue(_has_host_state(tail))
+
+    def test_falls_back_to_lru_order_once_no_pass_through_is_left(self):
+        core = _FakeTreeCore()
+        a, b, tail = _chain(core, 3)
+        _seed_host_lru(core, [tail, a, b])
+
+        # a and b are pass-through checkpoints; the tail goes in the fallback pass.
+        self.assertEqual(_drive(core, 3), [11, 12, 10])
+        self.assertEqual(core.evicted, [a, b, tail])
+        for node in (a, b, tail):
+            self.assertFalse(core.host_lru_lists[MAMBA].in_list(node))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
